newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Airbus says narrow body orders to test capacity.
newsitem.headline: Airbus says narrow body orders to test capacity.

text.p: New orders are expected in the next few weeks for Airbus Industrie consortium A319, A320 and A321 aircraft, Airbus senior vice-president, commercial John. L.Leahey told Reuters in an interview.
"It also means it will be very difficult to find space on the production line for single aisle aircraft during the next three years," he said.

"Discussions with some well-known Latin American airlines have passed the signed memorandum of understanding stage and we are hoping for some A319 and A320 orders to be placed in the next few weeks," he added.
He declined to comment further on the possible orders. The three narrowbody aircraft provide a family of single aisle twin-engined aircraft ranging from 145 seats on the A319 to 220 on the A321.
Leahey said discussions are expected to continue over the next few months with the Chinese authorities on proposals to build a 100-seat aircraft.
Earlier on Tuesday in Beijing, Aviation Industries of China (AVIC) announced it would take a 46 percent stake in the project.

The European consortium Aero International Asia, which includes British Aerospace and France's Aerospatiale - two companies also in the Airbus group - will take a 39 percent stake with the remaining 15 percent taken by Singapore Technologies Aerospace, the official Xinhua news agency said.

"The plane will be marketed as an Airbus aircraft and will provide us with a 100 seater plane. It is not just being built for the Chinese market, which is expected to take only 20 percent of potential sales," Leahey said.
The cockpit and other systems are being designed to ensure commonality with the existing single aisle range, "allowing pilots to fly all of the range within the same day.
